text:
The wind at the summit did not howl; it whispered, carrying the scent of pine and ancient stone. Lara collapsed onto a flat outcrop, her chest heaving as the last of the climb’s agony faded into a dull, throbbing rhythm. Below her, the world unspooled in layers of emerald and slate, the clouds clinging to the valleys like spilled milk. She closed her eyes, letting the silence wash over her, feeling the vastness of the sky press against her eyelids.

A shadow darted across her vision, sharp and sudden. She opened her eyes to see a crow perched on a jagged rock nearby, its head cocked as if studying her. It was a creature of stark contrast against the soft hues of the landscape. Its feathers were not merely dark; they were a deep, iridescent black, shimmering with hints of blue and purple in the sunlight. It let out a single, guttural croak, a sound that seemed to echo the finality of her ascent, before taking flight, disappearing into the azure expanse.

The color of a common crow is black.
